chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I mentioned Mut'ah (temporary marriage) to him, asking if she is from the four (permanent wives). So he said: 'Marry from them a thousand, for they are hired (temporary wives).'

key_terms.الْأَرْبَع: The four (referring to the four permanent wives allowed simultaneously)
key_terms.مُسْتَأْجَرَات: Hired (referring to the nature of temporary wives who are compensated)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Mut'ah and permanent marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal distinction between permanent and temporary marriage by describing Mut'ah women as 'hired' (musta'jirat), thereby exempting them from the restriction of four simultaneous wives applicable to permanent spouses. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that Mut'ah is a distinct contractual category with its own rules regarding polygyny and duration, separate from the standard marital framework.
